data.title: Looking for High Yields? Dividend Aristocrat Stocks to Watch, According to Analysts
data.description:
Dividend aristocrats continue to stand out for offering investors a steady stream of cash payouts. Hormel Foods (HRL), Realty Income (O), and Amcor (AMCR) rank among the top five Dividend Aristocrats to buy for high yield, according to TipRanks’ Dividend Aristocrat tool. Top analysts covering each stock consider them worth watching.

Realty Income stands out for its leading 5.86% dividend yield and 237.35% payout ratio. However, Hormel offers the biggest upside potential of about 28%.

Dividend Aristocrats are S&P 500 companies (SPX) with a 25-year-or-longer streak of annual dividend increases. Income-focused investors who also want growth exposure often favor these companies.

data.title: Murphy USA (MUSA) Raises Quarterly Dividend by 11%
data.description:
Murphy USA, which operates a chain of retail gas stations, has raised its quarterly dividend payment by 11%. The Arkansas-based company has declared a quarterly distribution of $0.72 per share, up 11% from its previous dividend of $0.65. The new dividend gives MUSA stock a forward yield of 0.54% The next dividend is payable on Dec. 1 to shareholders of record as of Nov. 4 this year.

Murphy USA has paid a quarterly dividend to shareholders since 2013. This is the fifth consecutive year that the company has raised its distribution, having paused increases during the COVID-19 pandemic. The latest increase still gives MUSA stock a modest dividend yield of less than 1%, leaving plenty of room for further increases to the distribution in coming years.

data.title: Why Is AI OKTO Stock (AIOK) Up 176% Today?
data.description:
AI OKTO (AIOK) stock rocketed 176% higher on Friday after the company announced an asset sale and a special dividend. The company started the positive news with the reveal that it has agreed to sell Dream Arrax, a 2015-built 5,000 cbm LPG carrier vessel, for $18 million.

Robin Energy (RBNE) will buy Dream Arrax from AI OKTO, with the deal expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. However, it first has to satisfy customary closing conditions. Investors will also note that Robin Energy is a company that is led by Petros Panagiotidis. Panagiotidis is the chairman and CEO of AI OKTO and Robin Energy.

AIOK Stock Special Dividend

Following the company’s Dream Arrax sale reveal, it announced a special dividend for shareholders. AI OKTO will pay a dividend of $3.50 per share via cash or additional shares of AIOK stock. The dividend is payable Nov. 25, 2026, to shareholders on record at the close of business on Nov. 2, 2026.

AI OKTO noted that the Nasdaq has required the company to place a due bill dividend on its shares. That’s because the special dividend represents more than 25% of the stock’s trading price. This applies special rules to stock purchases and sales during the due bill period. That means investors who buy shares during the bill period will receive the special dividend, even if the trades are settled after it. On that same note, investors who sell shares during the bill period will not receive the special dividend, even if the trades are settled after it.

AI OKTO said that the dividend will be taxable, even if investors receive it in the form of additional AIOK shares. Shareholders who want the cash dividend don’t have to take any extra steps. Those who want shares instead of cash have to elect to do so. The number of shares issued will be determined by the 5-day volume weighted average price of AIOK stock through Oct. 22, 2026.

Is AI OKTO Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, AI OKTO stock lacks significant analyst coverage. Instead, traders can gain insight into the company through the TipRanks technical analysis tool. The Overall Consensus for AI OKTO is Strong Sell, based on two Bearish indicators. (See AIOK Stock Forecast)

data.title: Canada’s MTY Food Group Raises Dividend 35% as Profits Accelerate
data.description:
Canada’s MTY Food Group ($TSE: MTY) has raised its dividend an impressive 35%. The Montreal-based company operates restaurant chains across North America, with most locations found in shopping mall food courts. Brands operated by MTY Food Group include Thai Express, Extreme Pita, Taco Time, and Yogen Früz.

Going forward, MTY Food Group said that it will pay shareholders a quarterly distribution of C$0.50 per share (US$0.35). That’s up 35% from a previous dividend payment per quarter of C$0.37. The new dividend is payable on Nov. 13 of this year to shareholders of record as of Nov. 3. The new dividend gives MTY stock a dividend yield of 6.43%.

data.title: Verizon (VZ) Stock: Is That 6.6% Yield Worth the Risk?
data.description: Verizon’s (VZ) 6.6% yield looks appealing, but I’m wary of the risk. The U.S. wireless and broadband provider is improving its operating performance. CEO Dan Schulman recently reiterated an “unwavering commitment to the dividend”. However, October’s SpaceX (SPCX) spectrum deal has changed how I view the income case. A cheap stock needs dependable cash flows, especially with this much debt. I’m bearish because that dependability now faces a credible long-term challenge.
data.author: Nikolaos Sismanis
